classification.difficultyReason: Plan suitable surveys for different purposes and account for the intended population and response reliability.

content.prompt: Here are some issues for which statistical information would help. Discuss how to go about collecting it.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A coffee-making machine manufacturer wants to study people’s colour preference for their machines.

answer.short: Sample answer: Survey a representative sample of potential customers, showing the available colours and asking which they prefer.
answer.worked: Identify the people likely to buy the machines and select a representative sample. Show everyone the same colour choices under comparable conditions and ask a neutral preference question, allowing other or no preference. Tally the responses for each colour.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A council wants to determine the best resources for their library to hold.

answer.short: Sample answer: Survey a representative sample of local residents about their library needs and examine borrowing and resource-use records.
answer.worked: Ask residents from different age groups and areas which library resources they need, including residents who do not currently use the library. Compare their responses with borrowing, reservation and other resource-use records to identify both current demand and unmet needs.

children.label: c
children.prompt: An employer of 10 000 people wants to determine their employees’ attitudes towards the company.

answer.short: Sample answer: Use an anonymous questionnaire with neutral questions, inviting all employees or a representative sample to respond.
answer.worked: Use the same neutral questions for employees across departments, locations and job levels. Keep responses anonymous so employees can answer honestly. Invite all employees, or select a representative sample, and check whether the responses adequately cover the different employee groups.
